pct.$comment: Here the `primary` ramp goes UP (lighter on hover/active), the opposite of the light theme. The reason is measurable, not aesthetic: in the dark theme `on-primary` is DARK, so darkening the background drives the label's contrast down instead of up — that once gave 3.45:1 on hover and 2.66:1 on active, below AA, with a green build. The same token is also text on a dark surface (the outline variant's label), and that needs a light step: blue.500 on `surface-100` gave 3.98:1.
pct.$comment-scrim: The veil, and here it has to be the ramp's endpoint rather than `slate.900`: the dark theme's page IS `slate.900`, so a veil of the same step would dim it by nothing at all. How translucent it is, and how far the page behind it is blurred, are the component's two other tokens — all three are the skin's to set.
pct.$comment-surface-inverse: The surface that answers the page rather than joining it — dark on a light theme and light on a dark one. It exists for the annotation kind of panel (the tooltip is the first): a surface a reader is meant to notice for a moment and then stop seeing, which the ordinary `surface` cannot be, being what the page is made of. The `on-` pair is not decoration here — an inverted surface is the one place where reaching for `pct.text` by reflex paints text the same colour as the box it stands in.
